title: Jammu and Kashmir — the complete guide
selection: Jammu and Kashmir had 31 places, 3 itineraries and 2 guides. This pack adds Srinagar's shrines, museum, gardens and hill fort, Jammu's temples and palaces, Vaishno Devi and Sudh Mahadev, Amarnath, the Martand and Avantipora ruins, Kheer Bhawani, Pampore and Dachigam, with 3 itineraries and 8 guides — researched from Incredible India (Ministry of Tourism) and Wikipedia, and carrying the current travel advisory.

HAZ1.claim: Hazratbal, Srinagar's white-marble shrine, holds the Moi-e-Muqqadas, believed to be a hair of the Prophet Muhammad.

evidence.quote: It embraces the holy relic known as Moi-e-Muqqadas – a strand of Prophet Muhammad's blessed beard.
the shrine's majestic white marble architecture and domed structure

SHA1.claim: The Shankaracharya (Jyoteshwar) Temple stands on 1,000 ft Gopadri Hill above Srinagar; tradition links it to Adi Shankaracharya.

evidence.quote: It sits proudly on the 1000-foot-high Gopadri Hill and is also known as Jyoteshwar Temple or Pas-Bahar.
certain people also believe that it was built in the 9th century by Adi Shankaracharya

SPS1.claim: The Sri Pratap Singh Museum, once a royal summer palace, holds artefacts from Jammu, Kashmir, Baltistan and Gilgit.

evidence.quote: It was built as the summer home for the royals who ruled Kashmir
particularly the regions of Jammu, Kashmir, Baltistan, and Gilgit

JAM1.claim: Srinagar's Jamia Masjid covers 13,600 sq m; its roof rests on hundreds of deodar-wood columns.

evidence.quote: Thus the space area of the mosque is 13,600 square metres
three turrets standing on lofty columns of deodar wood
The remaining interior of the Mosque has 346 columns 6.4 metres (21 ft) high

CHS1.claim: Chashme Shahi, built around a spring in 1632 by Ali Mardan Khan, is the smallest of Srinagar's three Mughal gardens.

evidence.quote: The garden was constructed around the spring by the Mughal Governor Ali Mardan Khan in 1632.
It is the smallest garden among the three Mughal gardens of Srinagar; the Shalimar garden is the largest and the Nishat garden is the second largest.

TUL1.claim: The Indira Gandhi Memorial Tulip Garden, about 30 ha on seven terraces above Dal Lake, is Asia's largest tulip garden; it draws hundreds of thousands in March–April.

evidence.quote: It is the largest tulip garden in Asia spread over an area of about 30 ha
consisting of seven terraces
between March and April 2023, the garden was visited by 365,000 tourists

HAR1.claim: Hari Parbat hill has a fort of 1808, a Hindu temple, mosques and a gurdwara; Akbar first fortified it in 1590.

evidence.quote: It is the site of the Hari Parbat fort , built by the Durrani Empire , and of a Hindu temple , mosques , and gurdwara .
The first fortifications on the site were constructed by the Mughal emperor Akbar in 1590
The present fort was built in 1808

BAD1.claim: Badamwari garden in Srinagar is in almond blossom in March, a spring highlight.

evidence.quote: Badamwari garden or Badam Vaer park is in in full bloom now.
Last week (second week of March)

DAC1.claim: Dachigam National Park, 20 km from Srinagar, is a former hunting ground now protected for wildlife; its name means 'ten villages'.

evidence.quote: That is the Dachigam National Park, 20 km away from Srinagar.
That’s why it’s called Dachigam which is ‘ten villages’ in Kashmiri.
having transformed into a critical sanctuary for wildlife conservation

RAG1.claim: Jammu's Raghunath Temple, begun under Maharaja Gulab Singh in the 19th century, has seven shrines.

evidence.quote: Its history dates back to the 19th century when Maharaja Gulab Singh, the founder of the Dogra dynasty, envisioned building a grand temple to worship Lord Rama.
comprising seven shrines dedicated to various Hindu deities

BAH1.claim: Bahu Fort stands on a rocky plateau about 325 m up, with gardens around it; legend credits Raja Bahu Lochan.

evidence.quote: Bahu Fort is situated at an elevation of about 325 metres, constructed on top of a rocky plateau.
Legend has it that Raja Bahu Lochan, the brother of Jammu's founder, laid the first brick of this fort
The expansive gardens surrounding the fort provide a perfect setting for a leisurely stroll

AMA1.claim: Amar Mahal, a red-sandstone palace, is now a museum with Pahari miniatures, including a 47-piece Nala–Damayanti series.

evidence.quote: Built in the 1890s, this red sandstone palace-turned-museum
including a rare forty-seven-piece collection depicting the tale of Nala Damayanti

AMA2.claim: Incredible India lists tickets at ₹10 (adults), ₹5 (children) and ₹50 (foreign nationals).

evidence.quote: Adults: Rs. 10/- per head, Children: Rs. 5/- per head, and Foreign Nationals: Rs. 50/- per head

MUB1.claim: The Mubarak Mandi palace sits on a cliff in Jammu's old city above the Tawi river.

evidence.quote: Perched majestically atop a towering cliff in the Old City
the palace presents a breathtaking vista of the serene River Tawi

PKH1.claim: Peer Kho is a cave shrine 20–30 ft deep on the Tawi, linked in legend to Jamvant; records trace it to the 15th century.

evidence.quote: This underground cave is twenty to thirty feet deep.
It is believed that this cave was a meditative abode for Jamvant
the Peer Kho Cave Temple traces its origins back to the 15th century A.D.

VAI1.claim: The Vaishno Devi cave shrine is at 1,585 m on Trikuta hill, 12 km from Katra and about 61 km from Jammu.

evidence.quote: Perched at an elevation of 1,585 metres (5,200 ft), the temple is situated 12 km from Katra on Trikuta hill, approximately 61 km from Jammu city.

SUD1.claim: Sudh Mahadev near Patnitop is an ancient Shiva shrine at 1,225 m; open 7 am–12 noon and 4–7 pm.

evidence.quote: Sudh Mahadev Temple in Patnitop, Jammu is an exceptional ancient shrine with over 2,800 years of history.
With an elevation of 1,225 metres above sea level
Opening time - 07:00 AM - 12:00 PM and 04:00 PM - 07:00 PM

AMR1.claim: The Amarnath lingam is a natural ice stalagmite in a 40 m cave at 3,888 m; the pilgrimage season lasts 20–60 days.

evidence.quote: The lingam is a natural stalagmite formation inside a 40 m (130 ft) tall cave at an elevation of 3,888 m
The annual pilgrimage season varies between 20 and 60 days.

AMR2.claim: Pahalgam is the gateway to the Amarnath cave.

evidence.quote: Pahalgam- the gateway to the sacred Amarnath cave

MAR1.claim: The Martand Sun Temple was built in the 8th century by Lalitaditya Muktapida and destroyed by Sikandar Shah Miri.

evidence.quote: It dates back to the eighth century CE and was dedicated to Surya
the Martand Sun Temple was commissioned by Lalitaditya Muktapida in the eighth century CE.
The temple was destroyed by Sikandar Shah Miri .

AVA1.claim: The Avantipora ruins are of two 9th-century temples to Shiva and Vishnu built by King Avantivarman.

evidence.quote: This site originally comprised two temples, one dedicated to Shiva and the other to Vishnu
built during the reign of King Avantivarman of the Utpala dynasty in the 9th century CE

KHB1.claim: Kheer Bhawani in Ganderbal is built over a sacred spring said to change colour; its mela falls on Jyeshtha Ashtami.

evidence.quote: The holy spring is known to change its colour with various hues of red, pink, orange, green, blue, and white.
The mela is during Jyeshtha Ashtami

PAM1.claim: Pampore, about 11 km from Srinagar, is Kashmir's saffron town; Kashmir saffron won a GI tag in 2020.

evidence.quote: Pampore is about 11 kilometres away from Srinagar city centre Lal Chowk .
it also known as Saffron Town of Kashmir
The saffron grown in the Jammu and Kashmir region has gained a GI tag in the year 2020

GUL1.claim: Gulmarg is one of the world's highest ski resorts; Apharwat peak (4,390 m) has Asia's longest ski slope.

evidence.quote: Gulmarg is synonymous with skiing
The majestic Apharwat peak, towering at 4390 meters, boasts the title of the longest ski slope in Asia.

K_SX1.claim: Srinagar, at about 1,585 m, is the summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir, set around Dal Lake.

evidence.quote: As the summer capital of this northernmost Indian state
Elevation 1,585 m (5,200 ft)

K_SX2.claim: The Mughal gardens — Shalimar Bagh, Nishat Bagh and Chashme Shahi — have terraced lawns, fountains and water channels.

evidence.quote: The Mughal Gardens, such as Shalimar Bagh, Nishat Bagh, and Chashme Shahi, are masterpieces of Mughal horticulture, reflecting Persian influences in their terraced lawns, cascading fountains, and colorful flowerbeds.

K_SX5.claim: The Shankaracharya Temple on its hill above the lake is reached by a 5.5-km road from Nehru Park; Incredible India advises against walking up because of bears.

evidence.quote: take the winding 5.5 km road from Nehru Park
It's best to avoid walking, as the area is inhabited by wild bears.

K_SX7.claim: Each spring Srinagar holds a Tulip Festival at what Incredible India calls Asia's largest tulip garden.

evidence.quote: Srinagar adorns itself with the grand Tulip Festival each year, showcasing the resplendent beauty of the largest Tulip Garden in Asia

K_SX9.claim: Try rogan josh, yakhni, gushtaba and the multi-course Wazwan, with kahwa or pink noon chai.

evidence.quote: Relish the melt-in-your-mouth 'Rogan Josh,' a lamb dish cooked in a rich yoghurt gravy
'noon chai' a pink creamy concoction infused with saffron and cardamom

K_DL4.claim: Shikaras, gondola-like boats with heart-shaped paddles, carry visitors across the lake and through channels to Nagin Lake.

evidence.quote: a shikara, a gondola-like boat propelled by heart-shaped paddles
explore the canal-like passages linking Dal to Nagin Lake

K_SB1.claim: Shalimar Bagh was laid out by the Mughal emperor Jahangir in 1619 and later extended under Shah Jahan.

evidence.quote: The garden was built by Mughal emperor Jahangir in 1619
In 1630, Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan ordered Zafar Khan, the then governor of Kashmir, to extend this garden further

K_SB2.claim: It is the largest Mughal garden in Kashmir, covering 12.4 hectares in three terraces.

evidence.quote: Shalimar Bagh is the largest Mughal garden in Kashmir.
Area 12.4 hectares (31 acres)
The Shalimar Bagh has three terraces

K_NB1.claim: Nishat Bagh was built in 1633 by Asif Khan, Nur Jahan's elder brother, facing Dal Lake below the Zabarwan range.

evidence.quote: The garden was designed and built in 1633 by Asif Khan, the elder brother of Nur Jahan.
Nishat Bagh is a Mughal Garden built facing the Dal lake, with the back drop of Zabarwan Range.

K_GU1.claim: Gulmarg lies in a cup-shaped valley of the Pir Panjal at 2,650 m, about 56 km from Srinagar.

evidence.quote: Gulmarg lies in a cup-shaped valley in the Pir Panjal Range of the Himalayas , at an altitude of, 2,650 m (8,690 ft) . It is located about 56 km (35 mi) from Srinagar

K_GU2.claim: The two-stage gondola runs from Gulmarg to Kongdoori and on to about 3,980 m on Apharwat; the stages take roughly 9 and 12 minutes.

evidence.quote: The first stage transfers from the Gulmarg resort at 2,650 m (8,694 ft) to Kongdoori Station
takes skiers to a height of 3,980 m (13,058 ft)
The first phase of the ride takes around 9 minutes while the second takes about 12 minutes.

K_GU3.claim: In winter Gulmarg is India's best-known ski resort, with snowboarding, heli-skiing and tobogganing.

evidence.quote: Skiers from across the globe descend upon Gulmarg, eager to carve their way down the world-renowned slopes.
embark on a heli-skiing adventure

K_PH1.claim: Pahalgam, at about 2,200 m on the Lidder River, means 'village of shepherds' and is the gateway to the Amarnath cave.

evidence.quote: Pahalgam ( meaning the village of shepherds in Kashmiri)
It is located on the banks of Lidder River at an altitude of 2,200 m (7,200 ft) in the Vale of Kashmir .
Pahalgam- the gateway to the sacred Amarnath cave

K_PH2.claim: Trout fishing, rafting and walks along the Lidder, apple and walnut orchards, and Betaab Valley are the draws.

evidence.quote: It's an angler's paradise, with trout teeming in the crystal-clear waters.
There are apple and walnut orchards waiting to be visited.
The Betaab Valley, immortalized by Bollywood film

K_JS3.claim: The monsoon weakens behind the Pir Panjal, so much of the Kashmir Valley's rain falls in spring; Jammu is hot, with summer highs up to 46°C.

evidence.quote: The effect of the monsoon diminishes in areas lying to the leeward side of the Pir Panjal , such as the Kashmir valley, and much of the rainfall happens in the spring season due to western disturbances .
with extreme summer highs reaching 46 °C (115 °F)

K_JS4.claim: As of October 2026 the UK FCDO advises against all travel to Jammu and Kashmir — including Pahalgam, Gulmarg, Sonamarg, Srinagar and the Jammu–Srinagar highway — except flying to and travelling within Jammu city; it warns of a continuing terrorist threat to civilians including tourists.

evidence.quote: FCDO advises against all travel to the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir (including Pahalgam, Gulmarg, Sonamarg, the city of Srinagar and the Jammu-Srinagar national highway), except for:
travel by air to and from the city of Jammu
travel within the city of Jammu
There is a continuing threat, towards Indian government targets and civilians including tourists and foreign nationals.

K_JS5.claim: The FCDO warns that curfews and restrictions can be imposed quickly and that British consular help in J&K is severely limited.

evidence.quote: The authorities can impose and lift curfews and other restrictions frequently and quickly.
The level of consular assistance that the British High Commission in India can provide in Jammu and Kashmir is severely limited.

K_JS6.claim: After the April 2025 attack many sites closed; on 16 February 2026 the Lt Governor reopened 14 — including Yusmarg, Doodhpathri, Peer Ki Gali, the Tulip Garden, Thajiwas Glacier and Wular — with Gurez, Athwatoo and Bangus to follow once snow cleared.

evidence.quote: Lt Governor Manoj Sinha on Monday ordered reopening of 14 locations in Kashmir and Jammu region.

As many as 11 tourist spots in Kashmir division, including Yousmarg, Doodhpathri in Budgam, Dandipora Park in Kokernag, Peer Ki Gali, Dubjan and Padpawan in Shopian, Astanpora, Tulip Garden in Srinagar, Thajwas Glacier, Hung Park in Ganderbal and Wullar/ Watlab in Baramulla will be reopened immediately.
Three sites in Kashmir division — Gurez, Athwatoo, Bangus and one site in Jammu region —Ramkund in Ramban will be reopened once snow gets cleared.

K_JS7.claim: In April 2026 Baisaran meadow above Pahalgam, site of the 2025 attack, was still closed, and so was Chandanwari.

evidence.quote: Baisaran meadow in Pahalgam continues to remain closed to visitors
Tourism stakeholders attribute the decline mainly to the continued closure of Baisaran and nearby attractions such as Chandanwari.

K_JS8.claim: Prepaid mobile connections from the rest of India do not work in J&K because roaming is barred for security reasons; bring a postpaid connection.

evidence.quote: Similarly, no prepaid mobile from the rest of the country works in the state due to security restrictions.
“The ban on all prepaid mobile services (roaming) is for certain security reasons and there is no plan to revoke this ban,”

K_JS9.claim: Srinagar's airport is about 12 km from the city at Budgam; Jammu's is about 8 km from the city.

evidence.quote: The airport is located about 12 km
The airport is located 8 km

K_JS10.claim: Since 6 June 2025 trains have run from Katra to Srinagar over the Chenab bridge, the highest rail arch bridge, at 359 m above the river.

evidence.quote: on 6 June 2025, with the launch of train services connecting Katra in the Jammu region and Srinagar in the Kashmir valley
With a deck height of 359 m (1,178 ft) from the river bed, the arch bridge is the highest

K_JS13.claim: The Amarnath cave pilgrimage is made in July–August; pilgrims must pre-register months ahead, using the Baltal (north) or Pahalgam–Chandanwari (south) route.

evidence.quote: traditionally performed by lakhs of people in July and August during the Hindu holy month of Savan
Pilgrims have to pre-register months in advance and are allotted quotas according to state .
Srinagar railway station for the north pilgrim route through Baltal and Anantnag railway station for the south route via Pahalgam-Chandanwari

K_JS14.claim: Vaishno Devi, on Trikuta hill about 12 km from Katra, is run by the Shrine Board; every pilgrim must register and carry an RFID Yatra Access Card.

evidence.quote: is 12 km from Katra on Trikuta hill
A pilgrim has to get registered for the Yatra & collect RFID based Yatra Access Card.
It is managed by Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Shrine Board since 1986.

K_JS16.claim: Wazwan, served at weddings and festivals such as Eid, is Kashmir's feast; noon chai, a pink salted tea, is the everyday drink.

evidence.quote: The most popular drink is a pinkish coloured salted tea called " noon chai ".
Wazwan dishes with rice, some vegetables and salad are prepared for weddings and special occasions like Eid.

K_JS17.claim: Jammu's food includes rajma chawal, kaladi cheese from Ramnagar, khatta meat and kachaloo chaat.

evidence.quote: Jammu’s speciality is in a simple preparation which is famous all-over North India, known as the “Rajma Chawal”.
Jammu is also renowned for its processed cheese, Kaladi (local Cheese), which is made in the Ramnagar region of the state.
Dive into the tangy goodness of Khatta meat
Don't miss the heavenly Kachaloo Chaat

K_JS18.claim: Look for pashmina, namdas (embroidered felt rugs), carpets, shawls and walnut-wood carving.

evidence.quote: in Kashmir , pashm referred to the raw unspun wool of domesticated Changthangi goats
Discover the intricate artistry of Namdas, wool carpets adorned with colourful and masterful embroidery
local weavers manufacturing beautiful Kashmiri shawls, carpets, gabbas, namdas and rugs
Some of the wooden and walnut wood handicrafts can be a rare collection for you to treasure for long.

K_JM1.claim: Jammu, the winter capital, spreads either side of the Tawi below the Shivaliks and is called the city of temples.

evidence.quote: It serves as the winter capital of the union territory of Jammu and Kashmir.
Jammu - the city of temples is surrounded by the Shivalik range to the north, east, and southeast while the Trikuta Range surrounds it in the northwest.

K_JM2.claim: The Raghunath Temple (1853–1860), with seven shikharas, is one of north India's largest temple complexes.

evidence.quote: is one of the largest temple complexes of north India, located in Jammu city
Maharaja Gulab Singh and his son Maharaj Ranbir Singh built the temple, during the period of 1853-1860.

K_JM3.claim: Bahu Fort, 5 km from the centre on the Tawi, holds the Bave Wali Mata temple — busiest on Tuesdays and Sundays — and the Bagh-e-Bahu garden.

evidence.quote: Situated 5 kms away from the city centre, Bahu Fort stands on a rock face on the left bank of the river Tawi.
Pilgrims flock the temple on Tuesdays and Sundays, regarded auspicious.
An extensive terraced garden, known as Bagh-e-Bahu, has been developed around the fort.

K_KT1.claim: Katra, 42 km from Jammu, is the base town for the Vaishno Devi trek of about 14 km.

evidence.quote: 42 km (26 mi) from the city of Jammu
Katra is the base camp for pilgrims visiting Vaishno Devi Temple .
while on the trek of 14 km

guides.title: Kashmir travel safety and advisories
guides.summary: What to check before you go.
guides.seoDescription: Before travelling to Jammu and Kashmir: the UK advisory, closures after the April 2025 attack, reopened sites, and mobile-connection rules.

body.intro: Read this first: conditions in J&K change quickly.

sections.heading: Advisories
sections.text: As of October 2026 the UK FCDO advises against all travel to Jammu and Kashmir; curfews and restrictions can be imposed quickly.

sections.heading: Closures
sections.text: After the April 2025 attack many sites closed; 14 reopened on 16 February 2026, but Baisaran and Chandanwari were still closed in April 2026.

sections.heading: Phones
sections.text: Prepaid connections from the rest of India don't work in J&K; buy a local postpaid SIM.

guides.title: Srinagar's Mughal gardens
guides.summary: Shalimar, Nishat, Chashme Shahi and Pari Mahal.
guides.seoTitle: Srinagar Mughal Gardens: Shalimar, Nishat & More
guides.seoDescription: Srinagar's Mughal gardens: Shalimar Bagh (1619), Nishat Bagh (1633), Chashme Shahi (1632) and their setting on Dal Lake.

body.intro: Three Mughal gardens line Dal Lake below the Zabarwan hills.

sections.heading: Shalimar Bagh
sections.text: Laid out by Jahangir in 1619; the largest, at 12.4 hectares in three terraces.

sections.heading: Nishat Bagh
sections.text: Built in 1633 by Asif Khan, facing Dal Lake.

sections.heading: Chashme Shahi
sections.text: Built around a spring in 1632; the smallest of the three.

guides.title: Kashmir in spring: tulips and almond blossom
guides.seoTitle: Kashmir in Spring: Tulip Garden & Almond Blossom
guides.seoDescription: Spring in Srinagar: almond blossom at Badamwari in March and Asia's largest tulip garden in bloom March–April.

body.intro: Spring is short and spectacular in Srinagar.

sections.heading: Almond blossom
sections.text: Badamwari garden is in full almond blossom around mid-March.

sections.heading: Tulips
sections.text: The tulip garden — about 30 ha on seven terraces — draws hundreds of thousands of visitors in March–April.

guides.title: Vaishno Devi yatra guide
guides.seoTitle: Vaishno Devi Yatra Guide: Katra to the Shrine
guides.seoDescription: Planning the Vaishno Devi yatra: registration with the Shrine Board, Katra 42 km from Jammu, and the 12 km climb to 1,585 m.

body.intro: One of India's busiest pilgrimages starts at Katra.

sections.heading: Getting to Katra
sections.text: Katra is 42 km from Jammu; trains also run from Katra to Srinagar since 2025.

sections.heading: The climb
sections.text: The shrine is at 1,585 m on Trikuta hill, 12 km from Katra.

sections.heading: Rules
sections.text: Every pilgrim must register with the Shrine Board.

guides.title: Amarnath yatra guide
guides.seoTitle: Amarnath Yatra Guide: Season, Routes & Safety
guides.seoDescription: The Amarnath yatra: a July–August pilgrimage to the 3,888 m ice-lingam cave via Baltal or Pahalgam, with registration and safety notes.

body.intro: A high-altitude summer pilgrimage that needs planning months ahead.

sections.heading: The cave
sections.text: The lingam is a natural ice stalagmite in a 40 m cave at 3,888 m.

sections.heading: Season and routes
sections.text: July–August, from Baltal or Pahalgam; pre-register months ahead.

sections.heading: Safety
sections.text: Check the current advisory; Chandanwari on the Pahalgam route was closed in April 2026.

guides.title: Skiing in Gulmarg
guides.summary: The gondola, the slopes and the season.
guides.seoDescription: Skiing in Gulmarg: the two-stage gondola to Apharwat, Asia's longest ski slope, and what winter brings.

body.intro: Gulmarg is India's best-known ski resort.

sections.heading: The gondola
sections.text: A two-stage gondola runs from Gulmarg to Kongdoori and on to about 3,980 m on Apharwat.

sections.heading: The slopes
sections.text: Apharwat (4,390 m) has Asia's longest ski slope.

sections.heading: Winter
sections.text: Snowboarding, heli-skiing and tobogganing are also on offer.

guides.title: Jammu city guide
guides.summary: Temples, forts and palaces in the winter capital.
guides.seoTitle: Jammu City Guide: Temples, Forts & Palaces
guides.seoDescription: Jammu, the city of temples: Raghunath Temple, Bahu Fort, Amar Mahal, Mubarak Mandi and Peer Kho, and when to visit.

body.intro: Jammu is the winter capital and the gateway to Vaishno Devi.

sections.heading: Temples
sections.text: The Raghunath Temple's seven shrines; the Bave Wali Mata temple at Bahu Fort.

sections.heading: Palaces
sections.text: Amar Mahal's Pahari miniatures and the Mubarak Mandi complex above the Tawi.

sections.heading: Weather
sections.text: Summers are very hot; Jammu is gentler in winter.

guides.title: Kashmir food and shopping
guides.seoTitle: Kashmir Food & Shopping: Wazwan, Saffron, Crafts
guides.seoDescription: What to eat and buy in J&K: Wazwan and noon chai, Jammu's rajma and kaladi, Pampore saffron, pashmina, namdas and walnut wood.

body.intro: Kashmir's feasts and crafts are reason enough to visit.

sections.heading: Kashmir
sections.text: Wazwan, the wedding feast; rogan josh, gushtaba and pink noon chai.

sections.heading: Jammu
sections.text: Rajma chawal, kaladi cheese, khatta meat and kachaloo chaat.

sections.heading: Buy
sections.text: Pampore saffron, pashmina, namdas, carpets and walnut-wood carving.
